attributes.board_name: New Mexico Board of Dental Health Care

rules.accepted_credit_types: Local/state/regional/national/international dental, dental hygiene, dental assisting or medical professional associations (using their approved CE program designations), US Dept. of Education-accredited institutions, federal/state agencies (e.g. military, VA), hospitals and clinics, Board-approved study clubs; other courses by Board approval. Live webinars count fully; ACCME courses max 8 h per triennium.
rules.carryover: CE earned after submitting renewal but before the license expires may be used for the next cycle; otherwise not stated.
rules.alternatives: Emergency deferral up to 4 months for extenuating circumstances; licensees practicing/residing outside the US are exempt for the period of absence (notify the Board before expiration).
rules.audit_note: Selected renewal applications are audited (request comes with the renewal notice). Keep CE records 4 years.
rules.new_licensee_rule: Pro-rated at 20 hours per year for those licensed less than 3 years; an initial license issued for less than a full year needs 20 hours for the first renewal.

topics.who: Course in ethics or jurisprudence incl. the NM Dental Health Care Act and Board rules
Dentists holding a federal DEA registration: pain management with controlled substances; new DEA-registered licensees within the first year of licensure
Current hands-on BLS/CPR (AHA, ARC, ASHI/HSI); max 3 h credit

rules.legal_basis: 16.5.10 NMAC (Dentists, Continuing Education Requirements); 16.5.1.15 NMAC; 16.5.57.11 NMAC; 16.5.11 NMAC
rules.rule_quote: Sixty hours of continuing education are required during each triennial…
rules.notes: Dental licenses expire every 3 years on June 30 (renewal postmarked by July 1). Current hands-on BLS/CPR (AHA, ARC, ASHI/HSI) required, max 3 h credit. Self-study (pre-recorded, with post-test) max 50%. Sedation/GA permit holders follow 16.5.15.20 NMAC CE.
